strictOrdering.description: First ask whether the image has real aesthetic force: rich meaningful colour, substantial accomplished painterly execution, composed figures, believable anatomy, high religious dignity, reverent emotion. The work must be beautiful in its own right, not just illustrated subject matter.

Must invite attention, contemplation and Catholic devotion instead of looking like a generic historical engraving, institutional document, illustrative diagram, wooden mediaeval panel, flat cartoon or mundane genre scene.
Exact or honestly contextual feast, saint, mystery or Bible subevent; distinctive subject naming; no incorrect event reuse, theological distortion or misrepresenting author / medium.

Institutional original verified, photographic copy true to object, commercial-rights verified, sufficient colour/size, clean uncropped master and appropriate mobile display. These cannot rescue an aesthetically weak picture.

prohibitions: Do not use weighted scoring where technical checks and correct subject can compensate for insufficient beauty.
Never convert a source discovery, SHA-verified JPEG, readable phone crop or matched event into a primary art recommendation.
Do not put rejected artists or user-rejected individual artworks back into any affirmative shortlist.
El Greco and Fra Angelico remain excluded for new selections; earlier Velázquez suggestions are on a prior-user-rejection hold pending explicit reconsideration.
Old Testament art requirements may be sparse or reused: the reduced coverage quota does NOT lower quality standard for an image that IS displayed.
Never auto-reject 101 current user-chosen records; preserve historical selections separately with any style conflict holds.
